title: Grounding Relation Analysis Schema
description: Structured analysis of grounding relations in philosophical arguments. Captures what grounds what, the type and formal properties of grounding relations, and the overall dependence topology.

analysis_id.description: Unique identifier for this grounding analysis run

ground.description: Description of the grounding entity (what does the grounding)

grounded.description: Description of the grounded entity (what is grounded)

relation_type.description: Type of grounding relation between ground and grounded

direction.description: Direction of the grounding relation (e.g., 'mental → physical', 'normative → natural')

level_change.description: Whether the grounding relation crosses levels of fundamentality

formal_properties.description: Formal logical properties of the grounding relation

irreflexive.description: Whether the relation is irreflexive (nothing grounds itself)

asymmetric.description: Whether the relation is asymmetric (if A grounds B, B does not ground A)

transitive.description: Whether the relation is transitive (if A grounds B and B grounds C, then A grounds C)

explanatory_power.description: Assessment of how much explanatory work this grounding relation performs

chain_position.description: Position of this relation in a grounding chain (e.g., 'terminal', 'intermediate', 'initial')

dependence_topology.description: Overall topological structure of dependence relations in the argument

derivative_levels.description: Description of derivative levels and their layering structure

well_foundedness.description: Assessment of whether the grounding structure is well-founded (e.g., 'well_founded', 'infinitely_descending', 'circular', 'undetermined')
